# Reference paths (black-box Move traces)

Engine: the reference engine (Brood War 1.16.1 rules), Fastest speed (42 ms a frame). Frames are game frames. The engine's own map data was read as Brood War.

Method: each unit is created at the start point (the engine places it at the nearest free spot), the map's own units are removed, and it gets one Move order to the target. The position of each unit is read every frame. The trace ends at arrival (the frame at which the order is no longer Move) or after 3000 frames.

- Arrival frame: the first frame at which the unit's order is no longer Move (not arrived: the order stayed Move for 3000 frames).
- Path length: the sum of the distances between the unit's centre on consecutive frames, up to arrival (pixels).
- Final distance: the distance from the last position to the target (pixels).
- Minitile check: the frames on which the unit's centre lies on an unwalkable 8x8 minitile (centre cell = position / 8), counted up to arrival. Counts are of walkability as the engine reports it; 0 means never.
- Random seed: 42 (the engine's value at map load). Each trace starts from a fresh map load and a single unit (except section 3).

## 5. Could not be run or is unresolved

- No trip from a height-2 (high) point around a cliff was found by the search: the pairs that met the detour and line tests were all height 0 to height 1. Points in section 4a are the usable cliff trip.
- Several start points of the cliff search (736, 512) and (640, 480) and (800, 544) do not move a unit in some cases (listed above). The cause is not known; the engine's move command reports no error. Only the section 4a Zergling trip is a clean detour result.
- The minitile check uses the unit's centre only, not its footprint; large units (Dragoon, SCV) were measured the same way.
- Arrival is the order ending, not a distance test: the crowd units in section 3 end up 0 to 43 px from the target.
